entries.originalText: O Lord, what is my trust which I have in this life, or what is my greatest comfort of all the things which are seen under Heaven?
entries.modernizedText: O Lord, what is my trust in this life, or my greatest comfort among all the things seen under Heaven?

entries.originalText: Is it not Thou, O Lord my God, whose mercies are without number?
entries.modernizedText: Is it not You, O Lord my God, whose mercies are without number?

entries.originalText: Where hath it been well with me without Thee?
entries.modernizedText: Where has it been well with me without You?

entries.originalText: Or when could it be evil whilst Thou wert near?
entries.modernizedText: Or when could it be evil while You were near?

entries.originalText: I had rather be poor for Thy sake, than rich without Thee.
entries.modernizedText: I would rather be poor for Your sake than rich without You.

entries.originalText: I choose rather to be a pilgrim upon the earth with Thee than without Thee to possess heaven.
entries.modernizedText: I would rather be a pilgrim on earth with You than possess heaven without You.

entries.originalText: Where Thou art, there is heaven; and where Thou are not, behold there death and hell.
entries.modernizedText: Where You are, there is heaven; and where You are not, there are death and hell.

entries.originalText: Thou art all my desire, and therefore must I groan and cry and earnestly pray after Thee.
entries.modernizedText: You are all my desire, and therefore I must groan and cry and earnestly pray for You.

entries.originalText: In short I can confide fully in none to give me ready help in necessities, save in Thee alone, O my God.
entries.modernizedText: In short, I can trust no one fully to give me ready help in need except You alone, O my God.

entries.originalText: Thou art my hope, Thou art my trust, Thou art my Comforter, and most faithful in all things.
entries.modernizedText: You are my hope, You are my trust, You are my Comforter, and most faithful in all things.

entries.originalText: All men seek their own;(1) Thou settest forward only my salvation and my profit, and turnest all things unto my good.
entries.modernizedText: All people seek their own;(1) You set forward only my salvation and my profit, and turn all things to my good.

entries.originalText: Even though Thou dost expose me to divers temptations and adversities, Thou ordainest all this unto my advantage, for Thou are wont to prove Thy beloved ones in a thousand ways.
entries.modernizedText: Even though You expose me to various temptations and adversities, You ordain all this for my advantage, for You are accustomed to test Your beloved ones in a thousand ways.

entries.originalText: In which proving Thou oughtest no less to be loved and praised, than if Thou wert filling me full of heavenly consolations.
entries.modernizedText: In that testing You ought no less to be loved and praised than if You were filling me with heavenly consolations.

entries.originalText: In Thee, therefore, O Lord God, I put all my hope and my refuge, on Thee I lay all my tribulation and anguish; because I find all to be weak and unstable whatsoever I behold out of Thee.
entries.modernizedText: In You, therefore, O Lord God, I place all my hope and refuge; on You I lay all my trouble and anguish, because I find everything I behold apart from You weak and unstable.

entries.originalText: For many friends shall not profit, nor strong helpers be able to succour, nor prudent counsellors to give a useful answer, nor the books of the learned to console, nor any precious substance to deliver, nor any secret and beautiful place to give shelter, if Thou Thyself do not assist, help, strengthen, comfort, instruct, keep in safety.
entries.modernizedText: For many friends will not profit me, nor can strong helpers aid me, prudent counselors give a useful answer, the books of the learned console me, precious possessions deliver me, or any secret and beautiful place shelter me, unless You Yourself assist, help, strengthen, comfort, instruct, and keep me safe.

entries.originalText: For all things which seem to belong to the attainment of peace and felicity are nothing when Thou art absent, and bring no felicity at all in reality.
entries.modernizedText: For all things that seem to contribute to peace and happiness are nothing when You are absent, and in reality bring no happiness at all.

entries.originalText: Therefore art Thou the end of all good, and the fulness of Life, and the soul of eloquence; and to hope in Thee above all things is the strongest solace of Thy servants.
entries.modernizedText: Therefore You are the end of all good, the fullness of Life, and the soul of eloquence; and to hope in You above all things is the strongest comfort of Your servants.

entries.originalText: Mine eyes look unto Thee,(2) in Thee is my trust, O my God, Father of mercies.
entries.modernizedText: My eyes look to You;(2) in You is my trust, O my God, Father of mercies.

entries.originalText: Bless and sanctify my soul with heavenly blessing that it may become Thy holy habitation, and the seat of Thy eternal glory; and let nothing be found in the Temple of Thy divinity which may offend the eyes of Thy majesty.
entries.modernizedText: Bless and sanctify my soul with heavenly blessing, so that it may become Your holy dwelling and the seat of Your eternal glory; and let nothing be found in the Temple of Your divinity that may offend the eyes of Your majesty.

entries.originalText: According to the greatness of Thy goodness and the multitude of Thy mercies look upon me, and hear the prayer of Thy poor servant, far exiled from Thee in the land of the shadow of death.
entries.modernizedText: According to the greatness of Your goodness and the multitude of Your mercies, look upon me and hear the prayer of Your poor servant, exiled far from You in the land of the shadow of death.

entries.originalText: Protect and preserve the soul of Thy least servant amid so many dangers of corruptible life, and by Thy grace accompanying me, direct it by the way of peace unto its home of perpetual light.
entries.modernizedText: Protect and preserve the soul of Your least servant amid so many dangers of corruptible life, and by Your grace accompanying me, direct it by the way of peace to its home of perpetual light.

entries.originalText: Amen.
entries.modernizedText: Amen.
